(1) the medial preoptic region of the male Syrian hamsters brain contains both substance P- and prodynorphin-immunoreactive neurons; (2) neurons of the medial part of bed nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract and posterodorsal part of medial nucleus of the bed nucleus project to the medial part of preoptic area; (3) these projection neurons contain both substance P and prodynorphins; and (4) these projections may play a modulatory role
substance P- and prodynorphin- containing neurons of the medial amygdala and bed nucleus of the anterior commissura project to the medial and lateral preoptic areas in the male Syrian Hamster brain.

substance P- and prodynorphin-immunoreactive neurons in the medial nucleus of amygdala and the bed nucleus of stria terminalis project to the medial part of medial preoptic area of the male Syrian hamsters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the neurochemical basis of sexual behavior.
the neuroanatomical basis of the regulation of male sexual behavior by opioid peptides and substance P.
the role of the medial pre-optic area of the Syrian hamster in the regulation of reproductive behavior, and the neurochemical mechanisms that mediate these effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the projections from the medial nucleus of amygdala and the bed nucleus of stria terminalis to the medial pre-optic area in the male hamster brain are predominantly peptiderglic and are mainly composed of prodynorphin- but not substance P-containing neurons.
the medial preoptic region receives projections from neurons in both the medial nucleus of amygdala and the medial bed nucleus of stria terminalis that contain either substance P or prodynorphins.
there is a direct pathway between the medial preoptic nucleus and the medial nucleus of amygdala and the medial bed nucleus of stria terminalis in male Syrian hamster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a reciprocal connection between the medial preoptic nucleus and the medial bed nucleus of stria terminalis and the medial nucleus of amygdala.
the medial preoptic nucleus is the major target of the medial nucleus amygdalae and the medial bed nucleus of stria terminalis, which are both major targets for the olfactory bulb.

the medial preoptic nucleus receives projections from the medial amygdala and the medial bed nucleus of stria terminalis, and the medial amygdaloid and medial bed nucleus neurons that project to the medial nucleus are immunoreactive to C-peptide and substance P.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the medial preoptic nucleus is an important site for integration of sensory information, and it is also a major output site of the amygdaloid complex.
